name: website-toolkit
description: Copy-paste website parts in plain HTML and CSS, themed by CSS custom properties.

format.part: An HTML file: a <!--sr:part {json} --> header, then one <style> block scoped to .sr-<name>, then the markup. Elements to fill carry data-slot="<name>".

probes: every form field has a label
every stat has a source line
no target smaller than 24 px with another target within 24 px (links inside running text exempt)

after a real Tab press, every focused element shows an outline of 2 px or more at 3:1 contrast against what lies just outside each of its sides, or a two-tone ring (an unshifted, unblurred band) whose tones differ by 9:1
text contrast of 4.5:1, or 3:1 for large text, against the nearest opaque background

parts.title: Navigation bar
parts.summary: Brand name plus links. Below 640 px the links fold into a menu that opens without JavaScript (details/summary).

slots.link: Each navigation link (text and href); add or remove li items. The links appear twice: once in the wide nav and once in the phone menu; keep both lists the same
slots.current: aria-current="page" on the link for the current page

a11y: Brand link has a text name
Current page marked with aria-current
Menu is a native details/summary: keyboard and screen-reader operable

parts.title: Breadcrumb
parts.summary: Shows where a page sits in the site. The last item is the current page and is not a link.
a11y: nav with aria-label="Breadcrumb"
Current item has aria-current="page"
Separators are CSS, not read aloud

parts.title: Split hero
parts.summary: Headline, one sentence and two actions beside an image. Stacks text-first on narrow screens.

slots.headline: The page's one claim, under about 60 characters
slots.image: img src and a real alt text, or alt="" if decorative

needs: An image (any aspect ratio; it is cropped to fill)
a11y: One h1 per page: change to h2 if the page already has one
Image needs alt text written for the page
Both actions are links styled as buttons, at least 44 px tall

parts.title: Statement hero
parts.summary: One very large sentence and a single action, no image. For a page whose claim is the design.

slots.statement: One sentence; the key words can be wrapped in <em>

a11y: One h1 per page
The focus ring is drawn in the paper colour, because the band is ink
The large type scales with the viewport but never below 2.2rem

parts.title: Feature grid
parts.summary: A heading and three to six short features, each a title and one or two sentences. Columns reflow from three to one.

slots.heading: Section heading
slots.feature: Each li: a short title (h3) and a sentence

a11y: Features are a real list
Heading levels: h2 then h3; adjust to fit the page

parts.title: Numbered steps
parts.summary: How it works in three to five numbered steps. The numbers come from an ordered list, so reordering renumbers them.

slots.heading: Section heading
slots.step: Each li: a short title and a sentence

a11y: Uses ol, so the order is announced
Numbers are CSS counters, decorative to sight only

parts.title: Stat row
parts.summary: Three or four large numbers, each with a label and its source. A number without a source line is not allowed by the check.

slots.stat: Each div: the number (dd), what it counts (dt) and where it comes from (small)

a11y: A description list, so each number is read with its label
Numbers use tabular figures

parts.title: Testimonial
parts.summary: One quotation, large, with the person's name and role. Use real words from a real person, with their permission.

slots.quote: The quotation, without surrounding quote marks
slots.name: Who said it

a11y: figure/blockquote/figcaption: the source is tied to the quote
Quote marks are CSS

parts.title: Pricing table
parts.summary: Two or three plans side by side, each with a price, what it includes and one action. One plan can be marked as the usual choice.

slots.plan: Each article: name, price, period, the list of what is included, and an action link
slots.featured: Add class sr-price__plan--main and the 'Most chosen' label to one plan

a11y: Each plan is an article with its own heading
The featured label is text, not colour alone
Prices include the currency and period in text

parts.title: Questions and answers
parts.summary: Questions that open to show their answers, with no JavaScript. Each one can be linked to by its id.

slots.heading: Section heading
slots.qa: Each details: the question in summary, the answer in p

a11y: Native details/summary: operable by keyboard and announced as expandable
The open/closed marker is drawn with CSS and also changes shape, not only colour

parts.title: Image gallery
parts.summary: A grid of images with captions. The first image can span two columns. No lightbox and no JavaScript.

slots.item: Each figure: an img with real alt text and a short figcaption

needs: Images; the sample ones are inline SVG placeholders
a11y: Every image has alt text; captions add what alt does not
Images are lazy-loaded except the first

parts.title: Call-to-action band
parts.summary: A full-width band with one sentence and one action, to close a page.
a11y: Text on the accent colour uses the accent-ink token, checked at 4.5:1 for the bundled themes

parts.title: Contact form
parts.summary: Name, email, an optional subject and a message, each with a visible label. Posts to any endpoint you set; there is no backend in this repo.

slots.endpoint: The form action: a URL that accepts a POST of name, email, subject and message (your own server or any form service)

needs: A form endpoint that accepts POST fields name, email, subject, message
a11y: Every field has a visible label tied by for/id
Required fields say so in text, not only with an asterisk
autocomplete set on name and email
Fields are at least 44 px tall

parts.title: Email signup
parts.summary: One email field and a button in a band, with a line saying how often you will write.

slots.endpoint: The form action: a URL that accepts a POST of email
slots.pitch: What people get and how often

needs: A signup endpoint that accepts POST field email
a11y: The field has a visible label
The promise of frequency is text the user reads before signing up

parts.title: Map and address
parts.summary: An OpenStreetMap embed (no API key) beside the address written as text, with a link to open the map. The text works even when the map does not load.

slots.bbox: In the iframe src: the box around your place as west,south,east,north longitudes and latitudes
slots.map-link: A link to the same place on openstreetmap.org

needs: Network access to openstreetmap.org for the map tiles; the address text works without it
a11y: The iframe has a title and is out of the tab order (a focused frame cannot show a focus ring); the visible Open in OpenStreetMap link is its keyboard equivalent and does more than the embed
The address is real text in an address element, so it can be read, copied and used without the map

parts.title: Or divider
parts.summary: A rule with a word in the middle, for separating two alternatives, such as two ways to sign in.
a11y: role=separator with aria-label, so the word is announced once as a separator
Capitals are letterspaced 0.08em

parts.title: Section mark
parts.summary: A short centered ornament between sections of long text: three spaced marks instead of a full rule.
a11y: An hr, so it is a real thematic break; the marks are CSS

parts.title: Footer with social links
parts.summary: Name, a short line, page links, social links with simple drawn icons and text names, and the year. Icons are fixed at 20 px by width/height attributes, so they stay small even without the stylesheet.

slots.social: Each social link: href to your profile and the network's name in text

a11y: Social links have visible text names; icons are aria-hidden
Icons are generic drawn marks, not official brand logos; swap in official assets if your brand rules require them

templates.title: Service business
templates.summary: A small service business: what it does, how it works, prices, questions, contact and map. Uses the sample copy as written.

templates.title: Event
templates.summary: A one-day event: the statement, the programme as steps, speakers' words, where it is, and a signup.

templates.title: Portfolio
templates.summary: An illustrator's portfolio in Spanish: a statement, the work, a word from a client, and a way to get in touch.

templates.title: Product launch
templates.summary: One product, one page: the claim, three features, the numbers with sources, plans and a signup.
